gaps.sentence: I ___ hours yesterday trying to fix the printer, and it still doesn't work.
gaps.hint: fixed phrase: to use time without any result
gaps.explanation: waste time means to spend time uselessly; the second clause shows there was no result.

gaps.sentence: She ___ very well in her end-of-year exams.
gaps.hint: collocation: to ___ well in an exam
gaps.explanation: do well in an exam is the standard phrase meaning to perform successfully.

gaps.sentence: A sudden clap of thunder ___ the silence.
gaps.explanation: break the silence is the fixed collocation for ending a quiet period.

gaps.sentence: The judge ___ the verdict after four hours of deliberation.
gaps.explanation: 'Deliver a verdict/judgement' is the legal collocation.

gaps.sentence: After six hours of talks, the two sides finally ___ an agreement.
gaps.explanation: reach an agreement/decision is the collocation; 'arrive' would need 'at', which is not in the sentence.

gaps.sentence: We stayed indoors because of the ___ rain.
gaps.explanation: heavy rain is the standard collocation; 'strong rain' is not used.

gaps.sentence: Everyone agreed the suggestion was utterly ___.
gaps.explanation: utterly ridiculous is the standard collocation; 'utterly' is used with extreme adjectives.

gaps.sentence: He ___ a serious accident on his motorbike last year.
gaps.explanation: have an accident is the fixed collocation for being involved in one.
